newsitem.title: INDIA: India depository says $300 mln shrs dematerialised. [CORRECTED 07:01 GMT]
newsitem.headline: India depository says $300 mln shrs dematerialised. [CORRECTED 07:01 GMT]

text.p: Shares dematerialised on India's National Securities Depository Ltd (NSDL) exceeded $300 million on Tuesday, the NSDL said.
Dematerialisation is immobilising of share certificates in a central depository. It removes the cumbersome and time consuming process of physical share transfers.
The NSDL, India's first depository started in November, is open to members of the National Stock Exchange which operates from more than 100 centres across India.

The $300 million dematerialised represent 80 million shares. Retail investors have requested to dematerialise about 500,000 shares and they have so far opened 2,037 beneficiary accounts with depository participants, the NSDL said. (Corrects to show 500,000 shares rather than 500,000 investors.)

"Indian institutions have started dematerialising their holdings and the FIIs (foreign institutional investors) have also made a beginning by one FII putting its request for dematerialisation," NSDL said in a statement.

Companies with 965.90 billion rupees in market capitalisation have signed agreements with the NSDL, but the market capitalisation of shares currently available for dematerialisation is only 476.90 billion rupees, it said.
These include Larsen & Toubro, Associated Cement Companies, Reliance Industries, Housing Development Finance Company and Asian Paints.

Bank of Baroda, ITC Bhadrachalam Paperboards and Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilisers were the other firms among a total of 27 that have signed agreements for dematerialising their stocks, the NSDL said.
The NSE has a total market capitalisation of 4,500 billion rupees.
